text: Regional sales managers at Adventure Works Cycles should genuinely only ever see their own specific territory's numbers. This is exactly the dynamic row-level security scenario Chapter Eleven spent an entire chapter building directly toward.

One single role, one single filter expression, matched against a real user-mapping table — every single manager assigned to it sees only their own region, consistently across all three report pages at once, since row-level security always filters the entire underlying model, never just one isolated page.

Validate everything thoroughly before you ever trust it with a real person. Confirm the filter genuinely works as expected, and that your mapping table's email format actually matches what the live service itself returns, before adding a single real manager to that role.
A nightly refresh schedule is genuinely realistic for a dashboard exactly like this one — this particular project was never scoped to need real-time, minute-by-minute data in the first place.

Share the finished app with precisely who the original scope actually intended, granting view-only access — genuinely nothing more than that, since this project never called for anyone outside leadership to edit or rebuild any part of it.

Security is fully configured, refresh is properly scheduled, and access now matches the scope exactly as intended. Lesson 93 closes out this entire course: actually presenting the finished dashboard to a real audience.
